safety-architecture.title: Defense-in-depth: Squadron flight safety architecture
body: A severe Martian dust storm front has been detected approaching Mawrth Vallis. Wind speeds are fluctuating violently, and ambient atmospheric dust density is climbing toward critical levels.
Both active drones of the IRIS exploration squadron are airborne: agile scout drone IZLŪKS «Sigma» and heavy surveyor KARTOGRĀFS «Delta». Each drone possesses distinct structural limits:
- **Scout drone Sigma:** Highly vulnerable to severe wind shear and rapid battery drain during turbulence, but unaffected by sensor dust.
- **Surveyor drone Delta:** Armored against wind, but highly vulnerable to fine electrostatic dust accumulation on its optical LiDAR aperture and camera lenses.

In this practicum, we integrate everything learned across Block 2 — `if / else`, compound logical operators (`&&`, `||`, `!`), multiway `switch` dispatching, and inline ternary operators (`?:`) — into a unified, layered flight safety controller.

archive.title: Defense-in-depth in aerospace flight computers
body: In aerospace engineering, flight safety systems never rely on a single monolithic decision check. Following the defense-in-depth paradigm, safety architectures are organized in strict hierarchical tiers: signal validation, threat classification, and emergency response dispatch.

When the Apollo Guidance Computer (AGC) encountered CPU overload alarms (the famous 1201 and 1202 alarms) during Apollo 11's lunar descent, its priority-based task scheduling dropped lower-priority telemetry display routines while preserving vital thrust-vectoring calculations without restarting the flight computer.

Similarly, on the Mars 2020 Perseverance rover and modern autonomous UAVs, sensor telemetry passes through cascading filters: rapid sanity bounds checks (`if / else`), fault status bitmasks, and discrete payload actuator dispatchers (`switch`). If any sensor fails or disconnects, the system must deterministically divert execution to a safe operational baseline rather than halt.
sources: David A. Mindell, 'Digital Apollo: Human and Machine in Spaceflight', MIT Press
NASA JPL, 'Mars 2020 Avionics and Flight Software Architecture Overview'

predict-storm-hazard.title: Composite storm threshold evaluation
predict-storm-hazard.task: What action will this safety validator output for wind speed 22 m/s, battery 65%, and dust alert inactive (false)? Predict before running.
predict-storm-hazard.hint: Evaluate the first condition: is (22 > 20 || false) true? Is battery 65 < 50 true? If the first if is false, proceed to else if.
predict-storm-hazard.explain: The first check evaluates `(22 > 20 || false) && 65 < 50`. While the left side is true, the right side (`65 < 50`) is false, so the composite `&&` expression evaluates to false. The execution advances to `else if (wind > 20 && battery >= 50)`. Here both `22 > 20` and `65 >= 50` are true, so `HOLD POSITION` is printed.

sigma-wind-guard.title: Subsystem 1: Sigma environmental monitor
sigma-wind-guard.task:
Program Scout drone Sigma's weather safety validator using `cin`, `if`, `else if`, and `else`:
1. Read wind speed `int wind` and battery charge `int battery` from `cin`.
2. If `wind > 18` OR `battery < 20`, print `EMERGENCY LAND` and a newline.
3. Else if `battery >= 50` AND `wind <= 12`, print `FLIGHT NOMINAL` and a newline.
4. In all other cases (`else`), print `CAUTION: REDUCE SPEED` and a newline.
sigma-wind-guard.hint: Write `if (wind > 18 || battery < 20) { cout << "EMERGENCY LAND" << endl; } else if (battery >= 50 && wind <= 12) { cout << "FLIGHT NOMINAL" << endl; } else { cout << "CAUTION: REDUCE SPEED" << endl; }`.
sigma-wind-guard.solutionNote: With input 22 and 80, the wind condition 22 > 18 triggers the emergency land directive immediately.

delta-sensor-dispatcher.title: Subsystem 2: Delta instrument router
delta-sensor-dispatcher.task:
Program Surveyor drone Delta's sensor router using `switch (sensor)`:
1. Read sensor code `char sensor` from `cin`.
2. If `'L'`, print `SENSOR: LIDAR ONLINE` and exit with `break;`.
3. If `'C'`, print `SENSOR: CAMERA ONLINE` and exit with `break;`.
4. If `'R'`, print `SENSOR: RADAR ONLINE` and exit with `break;`.
5. In all other cases (`default:`), print `SENSOR: UNKNOWN` and exit with `break;`.
delta-sensor-dispatcher.hint: Use `switch (sensor) { case 'L': cout << "SENSOR: LIDAR ONLINE" << endl; break; ... default: ... }`.
delta-sensor-dispatcher.solutionNote: Input 'L' matches the first case label and outputs SENSOR: LIDAR ONLINE.

find-safety-bug.title: Subsystem audit: The false alarm trap
find-safety-bug.task: Click on the line where natural language ambiguity created an alarm condition that triggers on every single execution.
find-safety-bug.hint: Examine line 7 carefully: what is the right-hand operand of the || operator?
find-safety-bug.explain: Line 7 reads `if (alert_code == 1 || 2)`. Because `2` is a standalone non-zero integer, it evaluates to boolean `true` regardless of `alert_code`! This triggers the evacuation alarm even during diagnostic checks when `alert_code` is 0. The check must be written as `if (alert_code == 1 || alert_code == 2)`.

assemble-sensor-packet.title: Subsystem 3: Telemetry packet pre-filter
assemble-sensor-packet.task: Arrange the program lines in correct order to read drone telemetry and filter corrupted data before routing.
assemble-sensor-packet.hint: Start with standard includes, declare variables, read input, verify packet validity with !ok, and branch based on drone identifier.
assemble-sensor-packet.explain: The pre-filter first checks `if (!ok)` to reject corrupt packets. Only when data integrity is confirmed does execution proceed to distinguish between Sigma (`'S'`) and Delta.

power-allocator-ternary.title: Subsystem 4: Dynamic LiDAR purge controller
power-allocator-ternary.task:
Use the ternary operator `?:` to assign Delta's LiDAR purge mode based on dust density:
1. Read dust concentration `int dust` from `cin`.
2. Use the ternary operator to choose power mode: if `dust > 60`, mode is `"PURGE"`, otherwise `"ACTIVE"`.
3. Print `LIDAR MODE: ` followed by the mode string and a newline.
power-allocator-ternary.hint: Write `string mode = (dust > 60) ? "PURGE" : "ACTIVE";` followed by `cout << "LIDAR MODE: " << mode << endl;`.
power-allocator-ternary.solutionNote: With input 75, dust level 75 > 60 activates the high-pressure purge cleaning cycle.

squadron-safety-controller.title: Capstone Project: Unified Squadron Safety Controller
squadron-safety-controller.task:
Construct the integrated mission safety controller combining `switch`, `if`, and `else`:
1. Read drone identifier `char drone` and flight metric `int metric` from `cin`.
2. Route on `switch (drone)`.
3. For case `'S'` (Sigma, where metric represents wind speed): if `metric > 20`, print `SIGMA: GROUNDED`; otherwise print `SIGMA: AIRBORNE`.
4. For case `'D'` (Delta, where metric represents dust level): if `metric > 50`, print `DELTA: SHELTERED`; otherwise print `DELTA: SCANNING`.
5. For `default:`: print `DRONE: UNRECOGNIZED` and exit with `break;`.
squadron-safety-controller.hint: Inside each case of switch (drone), place an if / else statement checking metric against that drone's specific threshold.
squadron-safety-controller.solutionNote: With input 'S' 25, case 'S' executes, finds wind 25 > 20, and grounds Scout drone Sigma.

predict-edge-cases.title: Unregistered telemetry signal prediction
predict-edge-cases.task: What output will the squadron safety controller generate if an unrecognized signal `'X'` with metric 10 is received?
predict-edge-cases.hint: Does 'X' match case 'S' or case 'D'? Which fallback branch catches unmatched selectors?
predict-edge-cases.explain: Because `'X'` does not match `'S'` or `'D'`, execution skips both branches and jumps directly to `default:`, outputting `DRONE: UNRECOGNIZED`. In mission software, every switch must contain a default branch to safely handle corrupted or unexpected input.

storm-evacuation-override.title: Bonus challenge: Planetary storm evacuation override
storm-evacuation-override.task:
Program the base-wide emergency evacuation override protocol:
1. Read storm severity index `int storm` and clearance flag `char clearance` from `cin`.
2. If `storm >= 90` OR `clearance == 'R'`, print `PROTOCOL: IMMEDIATE EVACUATION` and a newline.
3. Else if `storm >= 50` AND `clearance == 'Y'`, print `PROTOCOL: RETURN TO DOCK` and a newline.
4. In all other cases (`else`), print `PROTOCOL: STANDBY FOR UPDATES` and a newline.
storm-evacuation-override.hint: Use a cascading if-else structure with || for the highest priority emergency and && for the intermediate warning.
storm-evacuation-override.solutionNote: With storm index 95 and clearance 'G', the storm threshold 95 >= 90 triggers an immediate evacuation protocol.

recap.title: Block 2 summary: Autonomous decisions unlocked
body: Congratulations! You have completed Block 2: «LĒMUMI» (Decisions) of the IRIS mission course. Scout drone Sigma and Surveyor drone Delta are now equipped with robust, deterministic decision-making logic.

| Control construct | Syntax | When to select in flight software |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `if / else if / else` | `if (val > 10) ...` | Continuous numeric ranges, floating-point comparisons, multi-variable logic |
| Logical operators | `&&`, `\|\|`, `!` | Synthesizing telemetry flags and applying short-circuit safety guards |
| `switch / case` | `switch (code) ...` | Discrete integer or char commands; high-speed $O(1)$ jump table dispatching |
| Ternary `?:` | `cond ? a : b` | Compact inline value assignment or immediate stream formatting |

Notice a fundamental limitation in all programs written so far: each program runs once from top to bottom and terminates. In real aerospace flight computers, telemetry must be sampled and processed thousands of times every second without stopping.
In Chapter 13, we inaugurate **Block 3: DATI & CIKLI**, beginning with the `while` loop — unlocking continuous, iterative computation!
